title: India and Canada Launch Economic Dialogue, Signal Readiness for Investment Treaty Talks
excerpt: Finance Ministers Nirmala Sitharaman and François-Philippe Champagne concluded the inaugural India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue in Toronto, setting an aspiration to expand bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion by 2030.
body:
• India expressed readiness to begin negotiations on a Bilateral Investment Treaty with Canada at the earliest, according to the official joint statement.
  • Both countries set an aspiration to expand bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion (INR 4.65 lakh crore) by 2030, up from USD 8.66 billion in 2025.
  • The ministers discussed broadening UPI adoption in Canada through partnerships with Canadian payment service providers.
  • The dialogue builds on the March 2026 commitment by Prime Ministers Modi and Carney to conclude CEPA talks by end of 2026.

India and Canada took a significant step toward repairing their economic relationship on Wednesday as Finance Ministers Nirmala Sitharaman and François-Philippe Champagne concluded the inaugural India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue in Toronto.

The joint statement released by both governments signaled an ambitious agenda: India expressed its readiness to initiate negotiations on a Bilateral Investment Treaty at the earliest, and both sides set a shared aspiration to expand bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion — roughly INR 4.65 lakh crore — by 2030.

Building on a Political Reset

The dialogue builds on the commitment made by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting in New Delhi in March 2026, which included a shared pledge to conclude Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) talks by the end of the year.

Bilateral trade between India and Canada stood at USD 8.66 billion in 2025, a marginal increase from USD 8.4 billion the previous year. India exported USD 4.22 billion to Canada and imported USD 4.45 billion. The CAD 70 billion target would represent an eightfold increase from current levels, requiring sustained growth across multiple sectors.

The ministers exchanged views on macroeconomic developments and domestic policy priorities, and discussed ways to strengthen investment ties in sectors including energy, artificial intelligence, critical minerals, and resilient supply chains.

Pension Funds and Institutional Capital

A significant focus of the dialogue was the role of Canadian institutional investors in India. The ministers noted the substantial presence of Canadian pension funds — including CPPIB, OTPP, OMERS, and Sun Life — in the Indian market, and recognized that current tax relief provided by India has stimulated investment.

Sitharaman held separate investor roundtables and bilateral meetings with major Canadian institutional investors, urging them to expand long-term investment in Indian infrastructure, renewable energy, and digital projects. She also discussed opportunities in GIFT City-IFSC with executives of Indian public sector banks.

"Both Ministers discussed the importance of domestic tax legislation that provides stability and certainty to taxpayers in respect of their investments."

— Joint Statement, India-Canada Economic and Financial Dialogue

UPI, Remittances, and FinTech

In a development with direct implications for the Indian diaspora in Canada, the ministers agreed to support efforts to broaden the use of India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in Canada through partnerships with payment service providers. They recognized that such efforts could contribute to faster, more cost-effective cross-border payments and support bilateral trade, tourism, education, and small business growth.

The ministers also explored deeper collaboration on payments modernization, financial stability, FinTech innovation, capital markets development, and efforts to address financial crime. Both sides agreed to pursue engagement between relevant authorities on cross-border remittances and merchant payments.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the estimated 1.8 million people of Indian origin living in Canada, the dialogue carries practical significance beyond trade figures. Cheaper and faster remittances through UPI integration, stronger investment treaty protections, and a formal CEPA could lower the cost of doing business across both countries.

Sitharaman's Canada visit also included a fireside session hosted by the Canadian Club of Toronto and the Canada-India Business Council, and an interaction with the Indian diaspora community.

The ministers confirmed that the next Economic and Financial Dialogue will take place in 2027. Sitharaman will continue her nine-day trip with stops in Chicago, Asheville for the G20 Finance Ministers meeting, and New York for investor roundtables and a NASDAQ bell-ringing ceremony.
nri_angle: UPI integration in Canada could lower remittance costs for 1.8 million Indian-origin Canadians; investment treaty and CEPA would strengthen economic ties for diaspora entrepreneurs.
